title: THE OLD MAN AND THE SEA

paragraphs.en: The old man, Santiago, had been fishing alone for eighty-four days without catching a fish. A young boy had fished with him for forty days, but his parents sent him away after that. The boy still came to help carry the skiff and its equipment each day.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫圣地亚哥已经连续八十四天独自出海而一无所获。一个少年曾与他一起捕鱼四十天，但后来因父母的原因被送走了。尽管如此，那少年每天仍然来帮助搬运小船和装备。

paragraphs.en: Santiago was thin and marked by years, yet his eyes were bright and hopeful. "I could go with you again," the boy said. "We've made some money."
paragraphs.zh: 桑提亚哥身材瘦削，岁月在他身上留下了痕迹，但他的眼睛依然明亮而充满希望。“我可以和你一起去，”孩子说道，“我们赚了一些钱。”

paragraphs.en: He remembered how they had caught big fish every day for three weeks after eighty-seven days of no luck.
paragraphs.zh: 他想起在连续八十七天没有捕到大鱼之后的第三个星期里，他们每天都能钓到大鱼。

paragraphs.en: The old man taught the boy to fish, and he loved Santiago deeply. "No," Santiago replied. "You're on a lucky boat now; stay with them."
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫曾教男孩钓鱼，他对桑提亚哥有着深厚的感情。“不，”桑提亚哥回答说，“你现在乘的是条幸运的船；就待在这上面吧。”

paragraphs.en: "But remember how you went eighty-seven days without fish," the boy said, "and then we caught big ones every day for three weeks." Santiago acknowledged their past success but said, "I know you didn't leave because of doubt."
paragraphs.zh: “但别忘了你连续八十七天都没有捕到鱼，”孩子说道，“然后我们连续三周每天都能钓到大鱼。”桑提亚哥承认他们过去有过成功的经历，但说：“我知道你不是因为怀疑才离开的。”

paragraphs.en: "It was Papa who made me go," the boy explained. "I must obey him."
paragraphs.zh: “是我爸爸让我来的，”男孩解释说，“我必须听从他的命令。”

paragraphs.en: "I understand," Santiago said. "It's normal."
paragraphs.zh: “我明白了，”桑提亚哥说，“这是正常的。”

paragraphs.en: The boy felt his father lacked faith in Santiago. But Santiago believed they still had hope. "Yes," the boy agreed, "can I offer you a beer on the Terrace and then we'll take the stuff home?"
paragraphs.zh: 男孩觉得父亲对桑提亚哥缺乏信任。但桑提亚哥相信他们仍有希望。“是的，”男孩应道，“那我可以请你喝一杯啤酒吗？然后我们再把东西带回家。”

paragraphs.en: "Why not?" Santiago replied. "Between fishermen."
paragraphs.zh: “为什么不行？”桑提亚哥回答道，“鱼erman之间。”

paragraphs.en: They sat on the Terrace. Some fishermen mocked the old man, but he remained calm. Others, older fishermen, felt sad for him but kept their feelings hidden.
paragraphs.zh: 他们坐在阳台上。有些渔民嘲笑老渔夫，但他保持冷静。另一些年长的渔民为他感到难过，但把这种感觉藏在心里。

paragraphs.en: "Can I go out to get sardines for you tomorrow?" the boy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “明天我可以出去给你买沙丁鱼吗？”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "No," the old man replied. "Go play baseball. Rogelio will help me."
paragraphs.zh: “不，”老渔夫回答，“你去打棒球吧。罗杰利奥会帮我。”

paragraphs.en: "I want to serve in some way even if I can't fish with you," the boy said.
paragraphs.zh: “即便不能和你一起钓鱼，我也想以某种方式为你服务。”男孩说。

paragraphs.en: "You bought me a beer, so you're already a man," the old man responded.
paragraphs.zh: “你请我喝了一杯啤酒，那你已经是男人了,”老渔夫回答道。

paragraphs.en: "How old was I when we first went fishing together?" the boy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “我们第一次一起去钓鱼时我多大？”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "Five years old. You nearly died when I brought in a green marlin and almost destroyed the boat," the old man recalled.
paragraphs.zh: “五岁了。我带一条绿衫鲭鲨上岸时你差点送了命，还差点把船搞沉。”老人回忆道。

paragraphs.en: "I remember the tail slapping, the thwart breaking, and the noise of you clubbing him," the boy said. "I can still smell the blood."
paragraphs.zh: “我还记得那尾巴拍打的声音，横梁被撞断的响声，以及你用棍子击打他的声音，”男孩说道，“我还能闻到血液的味道。”

paragraphs.en: The old man looked at the boy with his sunburned eyes, feeling both pride and love.
paragraphs.zh: 老人用被阳光晒黑的眼睛望着男孩，心中充满了自豪与爱意。

paragraphs.en: The old man said, "If you were my boy, I’d take you out to gamble, but you’re your parents’ son and in a lucky boat." The boy asked if he could get the sardines and four baits. The old man replied that he had some left from earlier, stored in salt in a box.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫说：“要是你是我的徒弟，我会带你出去碰碰运气，但你毕竟是你父母的儿子，而且现在是好时机。”男孩问能否去拿一些沙丁鱼和四枚钓钩。老渔夫回答说，他之前还有一些剩下来的好歹可以用的，存放在一个装满盐的箱子里。

paragraphs.en: "Let me get four fresh ones," the boy insisted.
paragraphs.zh: “让我再拿四条新鲜的吧，”男孩坚持道。

paragraphs.en: "One," the old man said, his hope and confidence still strong but growing like a rising breeze.
paragraphs.zh: “一次，”老人说道，他的希望和信心依然坚定，正像逐渐增强的微风。

paragraphs.en: "Two," the boy said, and the old man agreed, adding, "You didn’t steal them?"
paragraphs.zh: “两条鱼，”男孩说道，老人点了点头，又问了一句：“你没偷走它们吧？”

paragraphs.en: "I would if I could," the boy said. "But I bought these."
paragraphs.zh: “我会做如果我能，”男孩说，“但这些东西是我买的。”

paragraphs.en: "Thank you," the old man replied, too simple to question humility but aware he had attained it without loss of pride.
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢，”老渔夫回答道，虽然这句话太过简单，不足以质疑他的谦逊，但他明白自己是凭借实力赢得了这份谦逊。

paragraphs.en: "Tomorrow will be a good day with this current," the old man said.
paragraphs.zh: “明天会有好运气，”老人说，指的是当前的水流。

paragraphs.en: "Where are you going?" the boy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “你要去哪儿？”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "Far out to come in when the wind shifts. I want to be out before dawn."
paragraphs.zh: “等风向转了再进港。我想天蒙蒙亮前就出去。”

paragraphs.en: "I’ll try to get him to work far out," the boy said, "so if you hook something big we can help."
paragraphs.zh: “我要设法让他往远海游去，”男孩说，“这样如果钓到一条大鱼，我们就有帮助了。”

paragraphs.en: "He doesn’t like working too far out," the old man noted.
paragraphs.zh: “他不喜欢离岸太远工作，”老人注意到。

paragraphs.en: "No," the boy said. "But I'll see what he can't—like a bird or dolphins—and get him to follow."
paragraphs.zh: “不,”男孩说道，“但我可以观察他看不到的东西——比如鸟或海豚，并让他跟着它们。”

paragraphs.en: "Are his eyes that bad?"
paragraphs.zh: “他的眼睛真的那么差吗？”

paragraphs.en: "He is almost blind," the old man admitted, finding it strange since he had fished turtles for years and kept good vision.
paragraphs.zh: “他几乎失明了，”老人承认道，感到有些奇怪，因为他多年来捕海龟视力一直很好。

paragraphs.en: "But you went turtle-fishing off the Mosquito Coast for years with good eyes," the boy pointed out.
paragraphs.zh: “但你多年来在蚊子海岸以敏锐的目光捕海龟，”男孩说道。

paragraphs.en: "I am a strange old man," the old man said.
paragraphs.zh: “我这个老头真怪。”老渔夫说道。

paragraphs.en: "Are you strong enough now for a truly big fish?" the boy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “你现在有足够的力量来捕一条真正的大家伙吗？”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "I think so, and there are many tricks," the old man replied. "Let’s take the stuff home so I can get the cast net and go after the sardines."
paragraphs.zh: “我想是这样的，而且还有很多技巧呢。”老渔夫回答道，“我们先把东西带回家，我拿上网兜再去追捕沙丁鱼。”

paragraphs.en: They carried the fishing gear from the boat. The old man bore the mast, while the boy held the wooden box containing the coiled brown lines, gaff, and harpoon. They placed the bait box and club under the skiff’s stern before heading to the old man's shack.
paragraphs.zh: 他们把捕鱼工具从船上搬下来。老人扛着桅杆，男孩则拿着装有卷起的棕色钓线、鱼叉和钩子的木箱。他们先把饵料盒和木棍放在小船尾部下方，然后前往老人的小屋。

paragraphs.en: Together, they entered through its open door. The old man leaned the mast against the wall, and the boy set down the gear beside it. The shack was made of tough royal palm leaves called guano, with a bed, table, chair, and cooking area on the dirt floor.
paragraphs.zh: 他们一起走进了那扇敞开的门。老渔夫把桅杆靠在墙上，男孩则把装备放在旁边。小屋由坚固的王冠椰叶建成，屋顶和墙壁都是用这种叶子搭建的。里面有一个土炕、一张桌子、一把椅子以及一个简陋的灶台。

paragraphs.en: On the walls hung pictures of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Virgin of Cobre.
paragraphs.zh: 墙上挂着耶稣圣心和科布雷圣母的画像。

paragraphs.en: "What do you have to eat?" asked the boy.
paragraphs.zh: “你有什么吃的吗？”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "Just some yellow rice with fish," replied the old man. "Do you want some?"
paragraphs.zh: “只是些鱼肉拌黄米饭，”老渔夫回答道，“你要来一份吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No, I'll eat at home. Do you need me to make a fire?"
paragraphs.zh: “不，我回家吃。你需要我生火吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Not now. I might cook it cold later."
paragraphs.zh: “现在不行。我稍后可能把它凉着吃。”

paragraphs.en: "Can I take the cast net?"
paragraphs.zh: “我能用一下抛网吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Of course."
paragraphs.zh: “当然。”

paragraphs.en: The boy realized they had sold the cast net and there was no rice or fish. The old man then said, "Eighty-five is a lucky number. Imagine bringing in a big fish over a thousand pounds."
paragraphs.zh: 小男孩意识到他们已经卖掉了抄网，没有了米和鱼。老人 then 说：“八十五是个吉利的数字。想象一下能捕到一条超过一千磅的大鱼。”

paragraphs.en: "Let me get the cast net and go for sardines," replied the boy. "Will you sit in the sun by the door?"
paragraphs.zh: “让我去拿拖网，再去捕些沙丁鱼吧，”男孩回答说，“你要不要坐在门口晒太阳？”

paragraphs.en: The old man retrieved yesterday’s paper from under the bed, explaining that Pedrico had given it to him at the bodega. "I’ll be back with sardines," he said, adding they could share them in the morning. He instructed the boy to tell him about baseball when he returned.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫从床下取出昨天的报纸，解释说佩德里科在杂货店给了他。他说：“我一会儿拿沙丁鱼来，我们可以明天一起享用。”他嘱咐男孩在他回来时给他讲讲棒球的事。

paragraphs.en: "Pedrico gave it to me at the bodega," the old man explained.
paragraphs.zh: “佩德里科在杂货店给我的,”老人解释道。

paragraphs.en: "I'll bring sardines and we can share them on ice," he said. "Tell me about the game."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我带沙丁鱼来，我们可以冰镇着分享。”“给我讲讲那场比赛吧。”

paragraphs.en: "The Yankees cannot lose," the boy replied confidently, but admitted his fear of Cleveland's Indians.
paragraphs.zh: “扬基队不会输的，”男孩自信地回应道，但承认自己还是有些害怕克利夫兰印第安人队。

paragraphs.en: "But have faith in the Yankees, my son. Think of DiMaggio," the old man advised.
paragraphs.zh: 但是要相信扬基队，我的儿子。想想迪马吉奥吧，”老渔夫劝道。

paragraphs.en: "Both Detroit Tigers and Cleveland Indians scare me," the boy confessed.
paragraphs.zh: “坦白说，我害怕底特律老虎队和克利夫兰印第安人队。”男孩说道。

paragraphs.en: "You must be careful or you'll fear even Cincinnati Reds and Chicago White Sox," the old man warned.
paragraphs.zh: “你可得小心点，不然就连辛辛那提红队和芝加哥白袜队你也怕了。”老渔夫警告道。

paragraphs.en: "Study it and tell me when I return," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“研究一下，等我回来告诉我你的看法。”

paragraphs.en: "Do we buy a lottery terminal with eighty-five? Tomorrow is the eighty-fifth day," the boy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “我们用八十五买彩票机吗？明天就是第八十五天了。”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "We can do that," the old man agreed. "But what about your eighty-seven record?"
paragraphs.zh: “我们可以这样做，”老渔夫同意道，“但你那八十七天的记录怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: "It could not happen twice. Can you find an eighty-five?" the boy inquired.
paragraphs.zh: “这种事情不会第二次再发生了。你能找到一个八十岁的吗？”男孩问道。

paragraphs.en: "I can order one," he replied.
paragraphs.zh: “我可以点一份。”他回答道。

paragraphs.en: "One sheet, two dollars and a half. Who can we borrow from?" the old man wondered aloud.
paragraphs.zh: “一张纸条，两块五毛钱。我们能向谁借呢？”老渔夫自言自语道。

paragraphs.en: "That’s easy. I can always borrow that," the boy said.
paragraphs.zh: “这很简单，我可以借来用。”男孩说道。

paragraphs.en: "I think perhaps I can too, but try not to borrow. First you borrow, then you beg."
paragraphs.zh: 我想也许我也能做到，但尽量不要借。先借，然后就得求人了。

paragraphs.en: "Keep warm, old man," the boy advised as he left for sardines.
paragraphs.zh: “老头子，多穿点衣服保暖。”孩子嘱咐道，然后离开了去买沙丁鱼。

paragraphs.en: When the boy returned, the old man was asleep in his chair under an army blanket. The boy noticed the old man's powerful yet very aged shoulders and strong neck. His shirt, patched many times, resembled a sail with faded patches from the sun.
paragraphs.zh: 当男孩回来时，老人正躺在椅子上睡着了，身上盖着一件军用毯子。男孩注意到老人虽然年迈但依然健壮的肩膀和有力的脖子。他的衬衫已经补了好几次，看起来就像是一面被阳光晒得褪色的帆。

paragraphs.en: Though his head was old, it lacked life when closed. The newspaper lay across his knees, held by his arm in the evening breeze.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他的脑袋已经老了，闭上时却显得没有生气。傍晚的微风中，报纸搭在他的膝盖上，被他的一只手臂轻轻托着。

paragraphs.en: The boy left him there, only to find the old man still asleep upon his return.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子留下他独自一人，等他返回时发现老人仍然睡在原地。

paragraphs.en: The boy woke the old man, placing a hand on his knee. "Wake up old man," he said gently. The old man opened his eyes and smiled briefly before asking, "What have you got?"
paragraphs.zh: 男孩轻拍老人的膝盖，唤醒了他。“老爹，醒醒。”他说着，语气温和。老人睁开眼睛，微微一笑后问道：“你抓到什么了？”

paragraphs.en: "Supper," replied the boy. "We're going to eat."
paragraphs.zh: “晚餐。”孩子回答，“我们这就吃吧。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm not very hungry," the old man responded.
paragraphs.zh: “我并不饿。”老渔夫回答道。

paragraphs.en: "Come on and eat," the boy urged. "You can't fish without eating."
paragraphs.zh: “来吃吧，”孩子催促道，“你不吃饭就不能钓鱼。”

paragraphs.en: The old man stood up, folding a newspaper and blanket. "Keep the blanket around you," the boy advised. "You'll need it while I'm alive."
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫站起身，折叠好报纸和毯子。“你把毯子裹在身上。”男孩建议说，“等我还活着的时候，你还会用得着它。”

paragraphs.en: "Then live long and take care of yourself," said the old man. "What are we eating?"
paragraphs.zh: “那么就多活几年，好好照顾自己吧，”老渔夫说道，“我们吃的是什么？”

paragraphs.en: "Black beans and rice, fried bananas, and some stew," the boy explained.
paragraphs.zh: “黑豆米饭、油炸香蕉和炖菜。”男孩解释道。

paragraphs.en: The boy had brought the food from the Terrace in a two-decker metal container. He also carried two sets of knives, forks, spoons, and napkins wrapped in paper.
paragraphs.zh: 小男孩从露台拿来了一只双层金属容器装的食物。他还提着两套刀叉、勺子和餐巾纸，都用纸包裹着。

paragraphs.en: "Who gave this to you?" asked the old man.
paragraphs.zh: “这是谁给你的？”老渔夫问道。

paragraphs.en: "Martin, the owner," replied the boy. "I thanked him already."
paragraphs.zh: “马丁，船主，”男孩回答说，“我已经向他道谢了。”

paragraphs.en: "I must thank him too," said the old man. "He's very thoughtful for us. Has he done this more than once?"
paragraphs.zh: “我必须也感谢他，”老渔夫说道，“他对我们很体贴。他这样做不止一次吧？”

paragraphs.en: "I think so," answered the boy.
paragraphs.zh: “我想是这样的。”男孩回答道。

paragraphs.en: "He should get something more than just belly meat from a big fish," the old man said. "He sent two beers, and I like the cans best."
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫说：“他应该从这条大鱼身上得到的不仅仅是肚子上的肉。”“他还送了两瓶啤酒，我最喜欢易拉罐装的。”

paragraphs.en: "But these are bottles of Hatuey beer, and I'll take back the bottles," the boy added.
paragraphs.zh: “这些是哈图耶啤酒瓶，我会把瓶子拿回去的。”男孩补充道。

paragraphs.en: "That's very kind of you," the old man remarked. "Shall we eat?"
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢你的好意,”老渔夫说道。“我们吃点东西吧？”

paragraphs.en: "I've been asking you to," the boy gently reminded him. "I didn't open the container until you were ready."
paragraphs.zh: “我一直在提醒你呢，”男孩轻声说道，“直到你准备好了，我才打开那个容器。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm ready now," said the old man, washing his hands. "I only needed time to wash up."
paragraphs.zh: “我现在准备好了，”老渔夫边洗手边说，“我只是需要点时间洗漱一下。”

paragraphs.en: The boy thought about where the old man had washed and wished he had water and soap here for him. He should get another shirt and jacket for winter, some shoes, and a new blanket.
paragraphs.zh: 小男孩想到老人洗澡的地方，希望能有水和肥皂给他用。他还应该再买件冬衣和夹克、一些鞋子，以及一条新的毯子。

paragraphs.en: "Your stew is excellent," the old man said after they began eating.
paragraphs.zh: “你的炖菜非常美味，”老人在他们开始进食后说道。

paragraphs.en: "Tell me about the baseball," the boy asked, changing the subject. "In the American League it's still the Yankees," the old man replied happily. "They lost today," the boy informed him.
paragraphs.zh: “给我讲讲棒球的事吧，”男孩问道，话题一转。“在美国联盟，扬基队还是最强的，”老人高兴地回答说。“他们今天输球了，”男孩告诉他。

paragraphs.en: "That means nothing," the old man said. "The great DiMaggio is himself again."
paragraphs.zh: “这没什么意义，”老人说道，“迪马吉奥又找回了他昔日的风采。”

paragraphs.en: The old man reminisced about Dick Sisler's powerful drives, saying they were unlike anything he had ever seen. He regretted not asking Sisler to join them on a fishing trip, and wished DiMaggio could have come too, as his father might understand their struggles.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫回想起迪克·西斯勒那强劲的击球，觉得那些球简直是他从未见过的。他后悔没有邀请西斯勒一起去钓鱼，还惋惜迪马吉奥没能一起来，因为他的父亲或许能理解他们所面临的困境。

paragraphs.en: "I would love to take DiMaggio fishing," the old man said. "They say his father was a fisherman."
paragraphs.zh: “我真希望能带迪马乔去钓鱼，”老人说，“他们说他的父亲是个渔民。”

paragraphs.en: The boy, named Jota, remembered when John J. McGraw used to visit the Terrace. The old man described how McGraw's mind often wandered to horses while managing baseball. Despite this, he acknowledged McGraw as a great manager.
paragraphs.zh: 男孩名叫乔塔，他记得约翰·J·麦格拉夫曾经常常来露台。老人描述了麦格拉夫在管理棒球时常常心驰神往于赛马的情景。尽管如此，他还是承认麦格拉夫是一位出色的教练。

paragraphs.en: "Who do you think is the greatest manager?" Jota asked, curious about Luque or Mike Gonzalez.
paragraphs.zh: “你认为哪位是 greatest manager？”乔塔好奇地问卢克和米格尔·冈萨雷斯。

paragraphs.en: "I believe they are equally good," the old man replied.
paragraphs.zh: “我相信它们一样好。”老渔夫回答道。

paragraphs.en: "And you are the best fisherman."
paragraphs.zh: “你可是最好的渔夫。”

paragraphs.en: "No, I know others who are better," the old man said modestly.
paragraphs.zh: “不，我知道一些更好的人，”老人谦虚地说。

paragraphs.en: "But there's only one you," Jota insisted.
paragraphs.zh: “但就你一个，”乔塔坚持道。

paragraphs.en: "Thank you. That makes me happy." The old man hoped a great catch wouldn't prove them wrong.
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢。这让我很高兴。”老渔夫希望这次大收获不会证明他们错了。

paragraphs.en: "If I'm still strong as I say, no such fish will come."
paragraphs.zh: “如果我像自己说的那么强壮，这样的鱼就不会再来了。”

paragraphs.en: "I hope not," Jota agreed. "You ought to go to bed now so you'll be fresh in the morning. I'll take these things back to the Terrace."
paragraphs.zh: “但愿如此，”乔塔附和道，“你现在最好去睡觉，好让明天精神饱满。我这就把这些东西带回观景台。”

paragraphs.en: The old man said, "Good night. I'll wake you in the morning."
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫说：“晚安。我明天早上叫醒你。”

paragraphs.en: "You're my alarm clock," the boy replied.
paragraphs.zh: “你是我的闹钟,”男孩回答道。

paragraphs.en: "Age is my alarm clock," the old man responded. "Why do old men wake so early? Is it to have one longer day?"
paragraphs.zh: “年龄就像我的闹钟，”老人回答说，“为什么老人都起得这么早？是为了多拥有一整天吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I don’t know," the boy said. "All I know is that young boys sleep late and hard."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”男孩说道，“我只知道年轻人睡得很晚，睡得也很沉。”

paragraphs.en: "I can remember those days," the old man said, adding, "I’ll waken you in time."
paragraphs.zh: “我记得那些日子，”老人说，又补充道，“我会及时叫醒你。”

paragraphs.en: The boy left. The old man ate in darkness, then took off his trousers and went to bed. He rolled up his trousers for a pillow, stuffed with newspapers.
paragraphs.zh: 男孩离开了。老人在黑暗中吃完了饭，脱下裤子上床睡觉。他把卷起的裤子当枕头，里面塞满了报纸。

paragraphs.en: Wrapped in a blanket, he slept on top of old newspapers covering the bed springs.
paragraphs.zh: 裹着毯子，他睡在覆盖着旧报纸的弹簧床垫上。

paragraphs.en: He fell asleep quickly, dreaming of Africa's golden beaches and high mountains. Each night, he lived along that coast, hearing the surf and smelling tar and oakum as he dreamed. Tonight, the land breeze’s smell came early, but he continued to dream of islands and their harbors.
paragraphs.zh: 他很快就进入了梦乡，梦见了非洲金色的海滩和巍峨的山脉。每个夜晚，他都仿佛身处那片海岸边，听着海浪声，嗅着沥青和破布绳索的味道沉入梦乡。今晚，陆地微风的气息来得特别早，但他依旧沉浸在对岛屿及其港口的梦境中。

paragraphs.en: No longer did he dream of storms or fights; his dreams were now filled with lions on the beach, playing like young cats in the dusk. He loved them as he loved the boy. The old man woke up, looked out at the moon, unrolled his trousers, dressed, and went outside to urinate.
paragraphs.zh: 不再梦见风暴或战斗，他的梦里现在全是海滩上的狮子，在黄昏中嬉戏，就像年轻的小猫。他对这些狮子的爱如同对孩子的爱。老人醒来后望了望月亮，褪下裤子，穿上衣服，走到外面小便。

paragraphs.en: Shivering from the morning cold, he walked up the road to wake the boy.
paragraphs.zh: 瑟缩着身子，他迎着清晨的寒意走上道路，去叫醒男孩。

paragraphs.en: The boy entered his house quietly, barefoot, and found the old man waiting by the light of the waning moon. He gently woke the sleeping boy, who turned to look at him. The old man nodded, and the boy quickly dressed.
paragraphs.zh: 男孩光着脚悄悄进了屋，只见老渔夫正沐浴在残月的微光中等候。他轻手轻脚地唤醒了睡梦中的男孩，男孩转过身来看着他。老渔夫点了点头，男孩迅速穿好衣服。

paragraphs.en: They walked together down the road to the old man’s shack. Along the way, other barefoot men carried their boat masts in the darkness.
paragraphs.zh: 他们并肩走在通往老渔夫小屋的路上，一路上还有其他赤脚的男子在夜色中抬着船桅。

paragraphs.en: At the shack, the boy took the fishing gear from the basket—lines, harpoons, and gaffs—and the old man carried the mast with its furled sail. They stopped for coffee at a place that served early morning fishermen.
paragraphs.zh: 在小棚屋里，男孩从篮子里取出了钓鱼工具——鱼线、鱼叉和钓钩；老渔夫则扛着帆收拢后的桅杆。他们在一家专门为早起的渔民提供咖啡的地方停了下来喝杯咖啡。

paragraphs.en: "How did you sleep, old man?" the boy asked as he prepared sardines and fresh baits.
paragraphs.zh: “老头儿，你睡得好吗？”孩子一边准备沙丁鱼和新鲜的饵料一边问道。

paragraphs.en: "Very well," the old man replied. "I feel confident today."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”老渔夫回答，“今天我感觉挺有信心的。”

paragraphs.en: "So do I," the boy said. "I'll be right back with your sardines and baits."
paragraphs.zh: “我也是，”孩子说道，“我马上回来给你带鱼饵和沙丁鱼。”

paragraphs.en: He left to fetch the supplies, walking barefoot on the coral rocks to the ice house where they were stored.
paragraphs.zh: 他赤着脚走上珊瑚岩，前往存放冰块的冰库取物资。

paragraphs.en: The old man drank his coffee slowly, knowing it would be his only meal for the day. He had grown bored of eating and never carried a lunch. His water bottle in the skiff was all he needed.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫慢慢地喝着咖啡，知道这将是他在这一天唯一的餐食。他早已对吃饭感到厌倦，从不带午饭。小船上那只水瓶就是他唯一需要的了。

paragraphs.en: The boy returned with sardines and two baits, wrapped in a newspaper. They walked down the trail to the skiff, feeling the pebbled sand beneath their feet. Together, they lifted the skiff and slid it into the water.
paragraphs.zh: 男孩带着沙丁鱼和两块鱼饵，用报纸包着，回来了。他们沿着小径走向独木舟，脚底感受到鹅卵石铺就的沙滩。两人合力抬起独木舟，轻轻滑入水中。

paragraphs.en: "Good luck old man," said the boy.
paragraphs.zh: “祝你运气好，老渔夫。”男孩说道。

paragraphs.en: "Good luck," replied the old man. He secured the rope lashings of the oars onto the thole pins and began to row out of the harbour in the dark. Other boats from nearby beaches were also setting sail, their oar blades dipping and pushing through the water silently.
paragraphs.zh: “祝你好运，”老渔夫回答道。他将桨绳固定在船架上，然后在黑夜中划出了港口。附近海滩上的其他船只也相继起航，桨叶悄悄地浸入水中，无声地划动着。

paragraphs.en: Occasionally, someone would speak in a boat, but most remained silent. The old man's skiff spread apart from the others as they exited the harbour mouth, each heading towards where they hoped to find fish. He knew he was going far out, leaving behind the land’s smell and entering the clean, early morning scent of the ocean.
paragraphs.zh: 偶尔有人在船上说话，但大多数人保持沉默。随着船只驶出港口，老渔夫的小船逐渐与其他船只分开，各自朝着他们希望捕到鱼的方向进发。他知道这次要远航，将陆地的气息抛在身后，进入清新而略带晨意的海风中。

paragraphs.en: As he rowed over a part of the ocean called the great well by fishermen, he saw phosphorescence from Gulf weed in the water. This area, at seven hundred fathoms deep, attracted various fish due to the current's swirl against the steep walls of the ocean floor. Here, shrimp and bait fish congregated, sometimes with schools of squid rising close to the surface at night for feeding.
paragraphs.zh: 当他划船经过渔民称之为“大漩涡”的海域时，看到水中浮游植物发出磷光。这片深达七百米的海域因洋流在海底陡峭壁面处形成的旋涡而吸引了各种鱼类。在这里，虾类和饵鱼聚集在一起，有时到了夜晚，鱿鱼也会成群结队地靠近水面觅食。

paragraphs.en: The old man felt the morning approaching in the darkness as he rowed. He heard the trembling sound of flying fish leaving the water and the hiss of their stiff wings as they soared away. He cherished these fish, seeing them as his main companions on the sea.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫在黑暗中划着船，感受到晨曦渐渐临近。他听到了飞鱼离水时颤抖的声音和它们硬翅滑翔时发出的嘶嘶声。他对这些鱼怀有特殊的感情，视它们为海上最主要的伙伴。

paragraphs.en: He pitied the small terns, always flying and searching but rarely finding food. Why did nature make such delicate birds when the ocean could be so cruel? The sea was kind and beautiful, yet it could be harsh.
paragraphs.zh: 他怜悯那些小海燕，它们总是飞翔觅食却鲜有收获。为何造物主创造了如此娇嫩的鸟儿，而大海却如此残酷？大海既温柔又美丽，却又如此无情。

paragraphs.en: He thought of the sea as "la mar," a term used by those who loved her. Sometimes people spoke ill of her, but they always said it like she were a woman. Younger fishermen, using buoys and motorboats, called her "el mar" and saw her as an opponent or a place to compete against.
paragraphs.zh: 他想到大海时称之为“la mar”，这个词被那些热爱她的人所使用。有时人们也会对她口出恶言，但总是像在谈论一个女人一样。年轻的渔民则用浮标和机动船称她为“el mar”，视她为对手或竞争的对象。

paragraphs.en: But the old man viewed her as feminine, someone who granted great favors or withheld them when needed.
paragraphs.zh: 但老人看待她的眼光中带着几分女性化的视角，认为她是那种在需要时给予巨大恩惠或加以保留的人。

paragraphs.en: Rowing steadily, he felt no effort since he maintained his speed well. The ocean's surface was calm except for occasional swirls from the current. As dawn began to lighten the sky, he realized he had rowed further than planned.
paragraphs.zh: 稳稳地划着船，他感觉毫不费力，因为他的速度保持得很好。海面平静如镜，偶尔有水流形成的旋涡。黎明的曙光渐渐亮起，他意识到自己比原计划划得更远了。

paragraphs.en: I worked the deep wells last week and caught nothing, he thought. Today I'll find where the schools of bonito and albacore are; maybe there will be a big one with them.
paragraphs.zh: 上周我打了一周的深水井，一条鱼也没捕到，他心想。今天我要找到金枪鱼和大青鲨成群的地方；或许它们中间会有条大鱼。

paragraphs.en: Before dawn, the old man had his baits out and was drifting with the current. He had three lines: one at forty fathoms, another at seventy-five, and two more in deeper blue water at one hundred and one hundred and twenty-five fathoms. Each bait hung head down, covered with fresh sardines that were hooked through both eyes to form a half-garland on the hook.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明前，老渔夫已经布好了钓饵，在海流中随波逐流。他一共用了三条钓线：一条在四十米深处，另一条在七十五米深处，还有两条则延伸到了更深的海域，在一百米和一百二十五米处。每根钓线上挂着头朝下的钓饵，这些新鲜的沙丁鱼穿过双眼钩住，形成了半环状挂在钓钩上。

paragraphs.en: The boy had given him two small tunas for the deepest lines, while he used a big blue runner and a yellow jack on the others. Despite their previous use, they remained in good condition and were enhanced by excellent sardines. Each line, as thick as a pencil, was looped onto a green-sapped stick to detect any pull or touch.
paragraphs.zh: 小男孩给了他两条小金枪鱼用于最深的钓线，而他自己则使用了一条大蓝马林鱼和一条黄色鲭鱼在其他钓线上。尽管这些钓具之前已经用过，但它们依然状况良好，并且因为配有优质的沙丁鱼而更加出色。每根钓线粗如铅笔，缠绕在绿色浸渍的木棍上，以便随时察觉任何拉力或触感。

paragraphs.en: He had two forty-fathom coils that could be fastened to spare ones, allowing for over three hundred fathoms of line if needed.
paragraphs.zh: 他备有两卷四十英寻的钓线，可以与备用钓线连接，必要时总共有超过三百英寻的钓线。

paragraphs.en: Now, the old man watched the dip of the sticks over the side of his skiff and gently rowed to keep the lines straight and at their proper depths. The sun rose thinly from the sea, and he could see other boats spread out across the current. As it grew brighter, the glare hurt his eyes, so he avoided looking directly into it.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，老渔夫注视着船舷外鱼竿的起伏，轻柔地划桨保持钓线笔直且处于合适的深度。太阳从海面缓缓升起，他可以看到其他渔船散落在水流中。随着光线逐渐变强，刺眼的光芒让他难以睁开眼睛，所以他尽量避免直接盯着太阳看。

paragraphs.en: He watched the lines descend into the dark water, ensuring they were straighter than anyone else's. At each level in the stream’s darkness, a bait waited exactly where he wanted it for any fish that swam there.
paragraphs.zh: 他注视着钓线缓缓沉入黑暗的水面，确保它们比任何人都要笔直。在水流的黑暗深处每一层，诱饵都恰好在他希望的位置等待着任何游过的鱼儿。

paragraphs.en: The sun had risen two hours higher, easing his eyes as he looked eastward. Only three boats were visible, far inshore.
paragraphs.zh: 太阳已经升高了两个小时，光线更加柔和，他向东方望去。只见近岸处有三艘小船。

paragraphs.en: All my life, the early sun has hurt my eyes, he thought, yet they are still good. In the evening, I can look straight into it without getting the blackness. It has more force then too.
paragraphs.zh: 他想，我一生中早上的太阳一直刺痛我的眼睛，但它们依然很好。到了傍晚，我可以直视它而不至于眼前一片漆黑。那时它的力量更大了。

paragraphs.en: But in the morning, it is painful.
paragraphs.zh: 但到了早上，那种疼痛依然让人难以忍受。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a man-of-war bird with long black wings appeared ahead. He saw it dive and heard flying fish splash out of the water, sailing desperately over the surface.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一只长着黑翅膀的军舰鸟出现在前方。他看见它俯冲下去，听到飞鱼从水中溅出，在水面拼命地滑行。

paragraphs.en: "He's got something," he said aloud. "He’s not just looking."
paragraphs.zh: 他钓上omething了,”他大声说道，“不只是在 LOOKING。”

paragraphs.en: He rowed slowly toward where the bird was circling, not hurrying but keeping his lines straight. He slightly crowded the current to move faster without losing his technique.
paragraphs.zh: 他缓缓划向那只鸟盘旋的地方，不急不躁，却保持船线笔直。他稍微催促了一下水流，希望能更快一些，却不至于破坏自己的技巧。

paragraphs.en: The bird rose higher and circled again, its wings motionless. Then it dove suddenly, and he saw flying fish spurt out of the water.
paragraphs.zh: 那只鸟飞得更高，又绕了一圈，翅膀一动不动。随后它突然俯冲下来，他看到一群飞鱼从水中跃出。

paragraphs.en: "Dolphin," he said aloud. "Big dolphin."
paragraphs.zh: “ Dolphin, ”他大声说道，“大 Dolphin。 ”

paragraphs.en: He shipped his oars and brought a small line from under the bow. It had a wire leader and a medium-sized hook, which he baited with one of the sardines. He let it go over the side and then made it fast to a ring bolt in the stern.
paragraphs.zh: 他收起浆，从船首下方取了一根小鱼线。这根线上装有一段钢丝引线和一个中号钓钩，他用其中一条沙丁鱼做饵。随后将鱼线抛下舷外，并将其固定在船尾的一个环形螺栓上。

paragraphs.en: Then he baited another line and left it coiled in the shade of the bow. Returning to rowing, he watched the long-winged black bird working low over the water.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，他重新装上鱼饵，让它盘绕在船首的阴影中。接着，他又开始划桨，注视着那只长翅膀的黑鸟低飞在水面上捕食。

paragraphs.en: The old man watched the bird dive for a flying fish, but its efforts were futile. Below, he saw dolphins cutting through the water, chasing the escaping fish. He thought there must be a big school of them, and they would soon drive the fish into the water.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫注视着海鸟猛扑向飞鱼，但徒劳无功。下方，他看到一群海豚在水中穿梭，追逐着逃窜的鱼群。他心想，一定有不少海豚，很快就会把鱼赶到水面上来。

paragraphs.en: He observed the flying fish burst out repeatedly, while the bird's attempts to catch them failed. The school had moved too fast, leaving him behind. But he hoped he might still catch a stray or find his big fish nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 他观察到飞鱼一次又一次地跃出水面，而鸟儿却一次次扑空。那群鱼游得实在太快，把他甩在了后面。但他仍希望能捕到一条漏网之鱼，或者发现他的大鱼就在附近。

paragraphs.en: His big fish must be somewhere in this vast sea.
paragraphs.zh: 他的大鱼一定在这片浩瀚的海洋某个地方。

paragraphs.en: Above, clouds rose like mountains, and the coast was just a long green line with gray-blue hills beyond. The water turned dark blue, almost purple. He saw red plankton filtering through the deep water and the strange light the sun cast now that it had risen higher.
paragraphs.zh: 上方，云层如山峦般堆积，海岸线只是一条长长的绿色线条，后面是灰蓝色的山丘。海水变得深蓝，几乎接近紫色。他看到红藻在深水中缓缓漂浮，并且阳光现在更高时投下奇异的光线。

paragraphs.en: Happy to see so much plankton, he knew fish were nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 见到这么多浮游生物他很高兴，知道鱼儿不远了。

paragraphs.en: The strange sunlight meant good weather, as did the shape of the clouds over land. But the bird was nearly out of sight. Only patches of yellow Sargasso weed and a Portuguese man-of-war, floating cheerfully with its long purple filaments trailing behind it, showed on the surface.
paragraphs.zh: 奇怪的阳光预示着好天气，陆地上空的云朵形状也如此。不过那只鸟已经几乎看不见了。只有几片黄色的萨加索海藻和一只葡萄牙帆船水母浮在水面，它们悠然自得地漂浮着，长长的紫色触须拖在身后。

paragraphs.en: "Agua mala," the old man said, referring to the dangerous water.
paragraphs.zh: “坏水，”老人说道，指的是这片危险的水域。

paragraphs.en: From his position, the old man observed tiny fish swimming between and under the bubbles created by a drifting filament. These fish were immune to the poison from the agua mala, unlike humans. When he worked a fish, welts and sores would appear on his arms and hands due to this poison.
paragraphs.zh: 从他的位置上看，老渔夫观察到一些小鱼在漂流的丝线产生的气泡之间和下面游动。这些鱼对agua mala释放的毒素免疫，而人类则不然。每当他捕获一条鱼时，手臂和手上就会出现红肿和水疱，那是毒素所致。

paragraphs.en: The iridescent bubbles, though beautiful, were deceptive. The old man enjoyed watching sea turtles eat them. He loved seeing the turtles approach, close their eyes, and consume the filaments whole.
paragraphs.zh: 这些五彩斑斓的气泡虽然美丽，却极具欺骗性。老渔夫喜欢看海龟吃它们。他欣赏着海龟靠近、闭上眼睛，然后将那些细丝整个吞下去的情景。

paragraphs.en: After storms, he walked on the beach, feeling the bubbles pop under his thick-soled feet.
paragraphs.zh: 暴风雨过后，他走在海滩上，感觉厚底鞋底下传来气泡破裂的声音。

paragraphs.en: He cherished green turtles and hawk-bills for their elegance and value but had a friendly disdain for loggerheads, which were large and slow. Despite not having mysticism about turtles, he felt sorry for them, even the giant ones that could weigh a ton. He ate turtle eggs to build strength, especially in May, preparing for big fish in September and October.
paragraphs.zh: 他珍视绿海龟和鹰嘴龟，欣赏它们的优雅与价值，但对那些体型庞大且行动迟缓的Logger头海龟则抱有一种友好的轻蔑。尽管他对海龟没有神秘感，但仍对他们心怀怜悯，即使是那些重达一吨的巨大海龟也不例外。他吃海龟蛋来增强体力，尤其是在五月，为九月和十月捕获大鱼做准备。

paragraphs.en: Each day, he drank shark liver oil from a drum in his shack, which was available to all fishermen. Most found it unpleasant, but he saw its benefits against colds and grippes, as well as for his eyes. Now, the old man noticed that the bird had circled again.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，他都会在小屋里喝鲨鱼肝油，这种油对所有渔民都是免费的。大多数人都觉得味道不佳，但他认为它能预防感冒和咳嗽，并且对眼睛有益。如今，老人注意到那只鸟又绕着他们飞了一圈。

paragraphs.en: He announced, "He’s found fish." No flying fish broke the surface, but as he watched, a small tuna leaped into the air, turned, and dove back into the water. More tunas followed, jumping in all directions, churning the water.
paragraphs.zh: 他宣布：“他找到了鱼。”尽管没有飞鱼跃出水面，但他注视着，只见一条小金枪鱼腾空而起，翻了个身，又重新扎入水中。随后，更多的金枪鱼从各个方向跳起，在水面上激起阵阵波澜。

paragraphs.en: The old man thought, "If they don’t travel too fast, I can get them." He watched the school of fish and the bird diving into the bait fish forced to the surface by their panic.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫心想：“如果它们游得不快，我还能追上。”他注视着那群鱼和鸟儿，只见那些鱼因恐慌而被迫浮到水面，鸟儿则一头扎了进去。

paragraphs.en: "The bird is a great help," he said. Suddenly, the line tightened under his foot, and he dropped his oars. Holding the line firm, he began to haul in the small tuna.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“这只鸟真是个好帮手。”突然，钓线在他的脚下绷紧了，他放下船桨。紧紧拽住钓线，他开始收起那条小金枪鱼。

paragraphs.en: As he pulled, the shivering increased, and he could see the blue back and golden sides of the fish before he swung it over the side into the boat.
paragraphs.zh: 他越拉，颤抖越发明显。鱼的蓝色脊背和金色侧身在他将鱼翻转过来放入船中时清晰可见。

paragraphs.en: The old man hit the fish on the head for kindness and kicked its still-shuddering body under the stern's shade. "Albacore," he said aloud. "He’ll make a beautiful bait.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫出于好意击打了大鱼的头部，然后把它仍在船尾阴影下，身体还在微微颤抖。“金枪鱼。”他大声说道，“这会是个漂亮的诱饵。”

paragraphs.en: He’ll weigh ten pounds."
paragraphs.zh: 他体重足有十磅。

paragraphs.en: He did not remember when he started talking aloud to himself, but it had likely been after the boy left. When fishing with the boy, they usually spoke only when necessary. They talked at night or during storms, considering unnecessary talk a virtue.
paragraphs.zh: 他记不清是从什么时候开始独自出声说话的，但估计是在孩子离开之后。和孩子一起钓鱼时，他们通常只在必要时才交谈。他们会在夜晚或遇到风暴的时候说话，认为不必要的闲聊是一种美德。

paragraphs.en: Now, alone, he often expressed his thoughts aloud without worrying about annoying anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，独自一人时，他常常大声说出自己的想法，不再顾虑是否会惹人烦扰。

paragraphs.en: The old man thought, "Now is no time to think of baseball; only one thing matters." He believed there might be a big fish near the school. He had caught just a straggler from the albacore that were feeding far out and fast.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫心想：“现在不是想棒球的时候；只有一件事重要。”他相信附近可能有条大鱼在游弋。刚才捕到的那条金枪鱼只是远处快速觅食的一群中的一个落单者。

paragraphs.en: Everything on the surface moved quickly northeastward.
paragraphs.zh: 海面上的一切都迅速向东北方向移动。

paragraphs.en: He could not see the green shore, but saw blue hills with white tops like snow-capped mountains, and clouds resembling high snow peaks above them. The sea was dark, and sunlight created prisms in the water. With his lines going straight down into a mile-deep ocean, he only saw the great deep prisms.
paragraphs.zh: 他看不见绿色的海岸，只见一片蔚蓝，山峦白顶如雪峰般耀眼，云朵仿佛高耸入云的雪山。海水深邃而幽暗，在阳光下，水面上闪烁着五彩斑斓的光柱。他的钓线直插一英里深的海底，只见到处都是深海中的光影折射。

paragraphs.en: The tuna, called by fishermen as such regardless of species, were back under the surface. The sun was hot, and sweat trickled down his back as he rowed. He considered drifting and sleeping with a line around his toe to wake him, but decided to fish well today, eighty-five days without success.
paragraphs.zh: 金枪鱼，渔民不管种类都这么称呼它们，又潜到了水面之下。烈日当空，汗水顺着他的脊背滴落，他划着桨。他曾想过顺流而下，靠在脚上拴根绳子来唤醒自己小憩一番，但最终决定今天要好好捕鱼，已经连续八十五天没有收获了。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, watching his lines, he saw one stick dip sharply. "Yes," he said softly, then shipped his oars carefully. Reaching out, he held the line gently between thumb and forefinger of his right hand.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，他盯着钓线看，只见一根竿子猛地弯了下去。“是它！”他轻声说道，随后小心地收起了浆。伸手一握，他用右手拇指和食指轻轻捏住了钓线上扬的一端。

paragraphs.en: There was no strain or weight, but a tentative pull this time. He knew it was a marlin eating sardines at the hook's point and shank, one hundred fathoms down.
paragraphs.zh: 没有丝毫紧张或负担，这次只是一丝试探性的拉力。他知道那是一条马林鱼在钓钩的尖端和柄部吞食沙丁鱼，深达一百英寻之处。

paragraphs.en: The old man carefully released the line from the stick with his left hand, allowing it to run smoothly through his fingers without putting any tension on the fish. He thought the fish must be enormous this far out at sea.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫用左手小心地松开了钓竿上的鱼线，让鱼线在手指间顺畅滑动，没有对鱼施加任何拉力。他心想，这鱼离岸这么远，肯定个头不小。

paragraphs.en: "Come on," he said aloud. "Make another turn and come back to eat them."
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，”他大声说道，“再转个圈回来吃掉它们。”

paragraphs.en: He felt a light pull, then a stronger one as the fish struggled with a sardine's head. Suddenly, there was nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 他感觉到鱼轻微地拉了一下钓线，随后力度加大了一些，因为那条鱼正在与一条沙丁鱼的头部搏斗。突然间，一切又归于平静。

paragraphs.en: "Come on," the old man repeated. "Just smell them. Eat them good now, and then there is the tuna.
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，”老渔夫重复道，“闻一闻它们。现在好好吃下去，然后再来点金枪鱼。”

paragraphs.en: Hard and cold, but lovely. Don’t be shy."
paragraphs.zh: 艰难而冷峻，但美丽。别害羞。

paragraphs.en: He waited, watching the line closely for any movement. Then came another gentle pull.
paragraphs.zh: 他紧盯着钓线，耐心等待任何动静。接着，又传来一阵轻微的拉扯。

paragraphs.en: "He'll take it," he said aloud. "God help him to take it."
paragraphs.zh: 他说着大声说道：“他会带走它的。”“但愿上帝能帮他带走它。”

paragraphs.en: But the fish did not take it. The old man felt nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 但是鱼儿没有上钩。老人感觉不到任何动静。

paragraphs.en: "He can't have gone," he said. "Christ knows he can’t have gone. He’s making a turn, maybe remembering something from before."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“他不可能走了。”“上帝知道他不可能走了。他可能正在掉头，也许是在回忆起之前的一些事情。”

paragraphs.en: Then came another gentle touch on the line, and the old man was happy.
paragraphs.zh: 接着钓线上又传来一阵轻柔的触碰，老人心里感到高兴。

paragraphs.en: "It was only his turn," he said. "He’ll take it."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“这只是我的一局。”“他会赢的。”

paragraphs.en: Feeling the gentle pull again, then suddenly a heavy weight, he let the line slip down, unrolling off the first of two reserve coils. As the fish moved away, slipping through his fingers, he still felt its great weight.
paragraphs.zh: 感觉到鱼又轻轻一拉，随后突然变得沉重起来，他让钓线滑了下来，从备用的两卷线中放出了一部分。随着鱼儿游走，仿佛在指尖溜走一般，但他依然能感受到它巨大的分量。

paragraphs.en: "What a fish," he said. "He has it sideways in his mouth now and is moving off with it."
paragraphs.zh: “这条鱼真大，”他说，“现在它把鱼头侧着叼在嘴里正游走了呢。”

paragraphs.en: He thought the old man would swallow the bait, but he didn't say it aloud. The fish was enormous, and the old man imagined it moving in the dark with a tuna across its mouth. Suddenly, the line stopped, but the weight remained.
paragraphs.zh: 他心想老渔夫可能会吞下鱼饵，但没有出声说出。那条鱼巨大无比，老人想象着它在黑暗中游动，嘴里叼着一条金枪鱼。突然，钓线停住了，但感觉依然沉重。

paragraphs.en: Then, the pressure increased as the old man let out more line.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，随着老人放出更多的钓线，压力逐渐增大。

paragraphs.en: "Take your time," he said softly. "Eat it well."
paragraphs.zh: “慢慢来，”他轻声说道，“好好吃。”

paragraphs.en: He hoped the hook would pierce the fish's heart and end the struggle. He prepared for the fight, securing the reserve lines to be ready with three coils of forty-fathom line in addition to his current one.
paragraphs.zh: 他希望鱼钩能刺中鱼的心脏，结束这场搏斗。为了做好准备，他加固了备用钓线，确保除了现有的钓线外，还备有三圈四十米长的钓线。

paragraphs.en: "Eat a little more," he whispered.
paragraphs.zh: “再多吃点吧，”他低声说道。

paragraphs.en: The old man wished he had the boy by his side. He was being towed by the fish, feeling like the towing bitt himself. Despite the strength of his line, he couldn't lift the fish an inch.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫真希望男孩在身边。他被鱼拖着走，感觉自己就像那根拖缆一样无能为力。尽管钓线非常结实，他也无法将鱼抬离水面一英寸。

paragraphs.en: The line became taut, beads of water jumping from it.
paragraphs.zh: 钓线绷紧了，水珠从上面跳起。

paragraphs.en: "Let me put the harpoon in you," he thought as the boat began to move slowly northwest.
paragraphs.zh: 他心想，随着小船缓缓向西北方向移动，自己得把鱼叉插进它身上了。

paragraphs.en: The fish moved steadily, and they traveled on calm waters. The other baits were still in the water, but there was nothing more the old man could do.
paragraphs.zh: 鱼儿稳步游动，他们在风平浪静的水面上前行。其他饵料仍留在水中，但老人已经无能为力了。

paragraphs.en: "I wish I had the boy," he said aloud. "I'm being towed by a fish, and I’m the towing bitt. But thank God he is traveling and not going down."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“真希望还有那个孩子。”“我被一条鱼拖着，而我是那根拖缆。但谢天谢地，它在游动而不是下沉。”

paragraphs.en: The old man pondered what he would do if the fish decided to go down or die, but resolved to act. He held the line tightly and watched its angle in the water as the skiff moved steadily northwest.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫思索着如果鱼儿决定下沉或死亡他该怎么办，但还是下定决心要采取行动。他紧紧握住钓线，观察着钓线在水中的角度，小船平稳地向西北方向驶去。

paragraphs.en: The old man thought the fish would eventually tire, but four hours later, it continued swimming out to sea, towing the skiff. "I hooked him at noon," he said, "and I've never seen such a large one."
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫原以为那条鱼最终会疲倦，但四个小时后，鱼仍在不停地向海中游去，拖着小船前进。“我中午钓上的这条鱼可真大啊，”他自言自语道，“我还从没见过这么大的鱼。”

paragraphs.en: He had pushed his straw hat down on his head, which was cutting into his forehead due to the pressure. Thirsty, he knelt and moved as far forward in the bow as possible, reaching for the water bottle with one hand. He drank a little, then rested against the mast.
paragraphs.zh: 他把草帽压低，顶在前额上，由于压力的关系，帽檐有些扎人。口渴难耐，他跪下身子，尽量向前移到船首，伸手去拿水瓶。喝了一小口水后，他又靠在了桅杆旁休息。

paragraphs.en: Seeing no land behind him, he thought it made no difference; he could always return using Havana's glow. With two more hours until sunset, he hoped the fish would surface before then or during the night or sunrise. Feeling strong and without cramps, he wished he could see the fish to understand its strength.
paragraphs.zh: 见不到陆地，他想这并不重要；他可以利用哈瓦那的灯光返回。还有两个小时日落，他希望鱼儿能在日落前、夜间或黎明时浮出水面。感到体力充沛且没有抽筋，他渴望能看到那条鱼，以便了解它的力量。

paragraphs.en: The old man watched the stars, noting that the fish had not changed its course or direction throughout the night. He felt cold as his sweat dried on his back and arms. During the day, he spread a sack over the bait box to dry in the sun.
paragraphs.zh: 老渔夫望着星空，发现那条鱼整晚都没有改变航向或方向。汗水在他背部和手臂上干涸，让他感到一阵寒意。白天时，他把一个麻袋盖在饵料箱上，让它在阳光下晾晒。

paragraphs.en: After sunset, he tied it around his neck, positioning it under the line across his shoulders for comfort.
paragraphs.zh: 日落后，他把它系在脖子上，在肩膀上搭一条线以增加舒适感。

paragraphs.en: He thought, "I can do nothing with him, and he can do nothing with me. Not as long as he keeps this up." He stood up briefly to urinate over the side of the skiff, checking the stars and his course.
paragraphs.zh: 他心想：“我对付不了他，他也无法对我造成威胁。只要他还这么坚持下去。”他站起身来，在小船上解手，并抬头查看了星星和航向。

paragraphs.en: The phosphorescent line showed straight out from his shoulders, indicating they were moving more slowly towards the east.
paragraphs.zh: 磷光线从他的肩部一直延伸出去，表明他们正逐渐缓慢地向东方移动。

paragraphs.en: He wondered about the baseball games in Havana and wished for a radio. Reminding himself to focus, he thought, "Think of what you are doing. You must do nothing stupid."
paragraphs.zh: 他想起哈瓦那的棒球比赛，多希望能有一台收音机。提醒自己集中注意力，他心里暗自说道：“想想你现在在做什么。你必须不做任何愚蠢的事情。”
